main_body: A small wooden bucket (about 12px wide, rows 6-14) with a brown rim, a thin olive/green slop strip at the opening, and a banded brown body with a dark base. The faint grey-blue shape above the rim (rows 3-6) is a ghost highlight or handle, not part of the body.
top_band: Light brown rim at rows 6-7, with an olive/green slop strip and a dark handle line at rows 7-8. It is only 1-2 rows tall and has no distinct top surface.
evidence: Reading one column down the middle, the rim and slop strip add up to about 2 rows, then the banded front face follows. The opening is not an ellipse and the inside cannot be seen. The slop is a thin green line across the rim, which does not count as an opening. Compared with the guide's ellipse-top barrel, this is a rim-only or front-elevation bucket. There is no lighter horizontal surface sitting above the front face and no eave shadow.

style.evidence: The bucket uses only about 3-4 tones, a light and a mid brown plus a dark brown outline, in flat horizontal bands. The outline is a tinted dark brown, which is fine. There is almost no grain, no plank texture and no per-stave highlights. At 2x beside the roofed well and the cheese stall, its tiles carry only 2-4 colours, which is far thinner than the references.
